page: Vultr vc2-1c-0.5gb is an entry-tier virtual machine within the Cloud Compute family. It features a single shared vCPU based on the Intel x86_64 architecture operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, along with support for AVX, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. System memory is constrained to 0.5 GB RAM, paired with 10 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are present on this instance.

In benchmark assessments, the shared single-core setup delivers modest computational throughput. Synthetic evaluation via stress-ng records identical single-core and multi-core scores of 508.19, placing its CPU capabilities in the lower decile of tested systems. Small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth reaches 52.84 GB/sec, reflecting entry-level bus performance. Given the shared CPU allocation and minimal 0.5 GB memory footprint, operations face strict ceiling constraints under memory pressure or multi-threaded task requirements.

From a resource allocation perspective, this server prioritizes minimal baseline operational costs over computational speed. The provision of fast local NVMe storage offsets basic disk I/O bottlenecks, though memory constraints prevent running heavy software stacks. Appropriate workloads include lightweight network utilities, low-traffic static reverse proxies, micro-services, simple automated scripts, and test environments with small operational footprints.
